source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lebanon, Ohio campus publishes 12 megawatts of IT capacity, the largest figure any Ohio data center reports, and small against the multi-hundred-megawatt clusters AI training now requires.

Ohio's published data center load totals 60.4 megawatts across 77 mapped facilities, and only 8 of those report power figures at all. One campus therefore accounts for 20 percent of the state total. That concentration says as much about which operators disclose capacity as about where capacity actually sits. The 400,000 square feet of technical space against 12 megawatts works out to roughly 30 watts per square foot, and at an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack the site would hold about 300 racks, though that rack figure is a modeling assumption rather than a published number.

The campus holds SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes certifications, which qualify it to host regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, and federal contexts. Those are compliance credentials, not compute credentials. They establish that the building can be trusted with sensitive data, not that it can be fed enough power to train a frontier model.

What the data leaves out is decisive. There is no grid interconnection capacity, no power source, no announced expansion, no tenant list, and no pricing. The suitability score of 58 names announced expansion as its one missing input. Whether this site matters to AI scaling depends on whether the grid serving Lebanon can deliver sustained high-density load and whether CyrusOne intends to grow here, and neither is published.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
